newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pan-German May adjusted unemployment rises 56,000.
newsitem.headline: Pan-German May adjusted unemployment rises 56,000.

text.p: German unemployment rose 56,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.358 million in May, the Federal Labour Office said on Friday.
The unemployment rate, which is based on unadjusted data, fell to 11.1 percent, compared with 11.3 percent in April.
West German adjusted unemployment rose by 25,000 to 3.042 million. The unemployment rate in west Germany was 9.6 percent, compared to 8.7 percent a month ago.
In the former communist east Germany, the adjusted jobless total increased by 30,000 to 1.316 million, and its unemployment rate was 17.2, up from 17.5 percent in April.
Federal Labour Office President Bernhard Jagoda said the economy in May was not growing fast enough to revive Germany's flagging jobs market.
"The seasonal revival in the German jobs market stopped in May," he said. "As before the driving forces of the economy are insufficient to bring about a turnaround in the jobs market."
